planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Lucky series lantana is bred for a compact, uniform, mounding habit well suited to containers and small-space plantings.

directions: Plant transplants after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Lucky series lantana is bred for a compact, uniform, mounding habit well suited to containers and small-space plantings. Clusters of small, brightly colored flowers in shades of yellow, pink, red-orange, and bicolor tones cover a dense, compact mound smaller and more uniform than older lantana selections, blooming continuously from late spring through frost and drawing butterflies and hummingbirds throughout the season. Extremely heat- and drought-tolerant once established, it thrives through the hottest, most humid part of summer with minimal care, tolerating poor soil and neglect far better than most bedding plants. It behaves as a root-hardy perennial in zones 8-11, dying back to the ground in a hard freeze and resprouting from the base the following spring, or is grown as a heat-loving annual further north.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Pow Wow Wild Berry coneflower is a compact, seed-grown selection that flowers reliably in its first year from an early start.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Pow Wow Wild Berry coneflower is a compact, seed-grown selection that flowers reliably in its first year from an early start. Vivid, rich magenta-pink flowers with a prominent orange-brown central cone cover a compact, well-branched plant bred for uniform seed-grown performance, an All-America Selections winner recognized for its unusually intense flower color and heavy first-year bloom compared to older seed-grown coneflower strains. Like other purple coneflowers it is an important native pollinator plant, drawing bees and butterflies through a long summer bloom season and providing seed for goldfinches and other birds if spent flower heads are left standing into fall and winter. Deadhead for continued bloom through summer, or leave the last flush of seed heads for winter bird interest, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Start transplants or plant container-grown stock in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Oranges and Lemons blanket flower is short-lived like most gaillardia and benefits from being allowed to self-sow to maintain the planting.

directions: Start transplants or plant container-grown stock in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Oranges and Lemons blanket flower is short-lived like most gaillardia and benefits from being allowed to self-sow to maintain the planting. Warm, glowing flowers open bright golden-yellow at the tips fading through orange to a soft apricot center, a smooth color gradient rather than the sharp banded bicolor pattern of the wild species, giving each bloom a warm, sunset-like glow that blooms continuously from early summer through frost. Extremely heat- and drought-tolerant once established, it thrives on poor, lean, well-drained soil and struggles in rich, moist, or heavily fertilized ground, making it a strong choice for a xeriscape border or gravel garden. Deadhead spent flowers to prolong bloom, and expect the plant to be relatively short-lived (two to three years), relying on self-sown seedlings to maintain the planting over time.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Start transplants or plant container-grown divisions in spring in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; Purrsian Blue catmint is a compact, mounding selection that tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil once established.

directions: Start transplants or plant container-grown divisions in spring in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; Purrsian Blue catmint is a compact, mounding selection that tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil once established. Aromatic, gray-green foliage forms a tidy, dense, compact mound smothered in spikes of vivid true-blue flowers from late spring through summer, a richer, deeper blue than many older catmint cultivars, and its compact size fits more easily into a small border or container than the larger, sprawling 'Six Hills Giant' or 'Walker's Low.' A magnet for bees throughout its long bloom season, it is deer- and rabbit-resistant and needs no fertilizer or supplemental water once established in well-drained soil. Shear the plant back by about a third after the first flush of bloom to encourage a tidy rebloom through late summer and fall.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes
